messages:
marta: Kickoff: splitting out the in-process session-batcher into a standalone BatchPool service. Goal: reduce runtime complexity, unify batching policies, and make cross-service batching observable. Thinking high-level timeline + migration strategy today.

nk: Strong +1. The in-process batcher has grown crufty with lots of special-cases. Externalizing should let us standardize backpressure and quota handling.

sam: Biggest worry is tail latency for small interactive requests. How do we keep p50/p95 unaffected while moving batching across IPC?

ryan: Two parts: 1) colocated fast-path for hotspot tenants (sidecar-ish) 2) TTL cache for recent batch decisions in the runtime to avoid roundtrip for ultra-low-latency paths. Also use unix sockets for minimal syscall overhead.

marta: Agreed. Proposal: BatchPool service exposes a small API: /enqueue (async, returns token), /status (poll by token), and /hint (sync) for the fast-path decisions. Runtime will default to hint when present.

nk: API sketch:```json
{ "tenant": "string", "model": "string", "seq_len": 64, "payload_size": 800 }
```Response for hint: { "batch_id": "string", "delay_ms": 12, "cache_ttl_ms": 100 }

sam: We should also support a synchronous decision API for callers that can't do polling. Maybe /decide that either returns immediate result or a short-delay token.

ryan: Good call. /decide will be limited to X QPS per runtime instance to avoid burdening the control plane. Otherwise we fall back to /enqueue. Rate limits configurable.

marta: Migration plan draft:
1) Build BatchPool PoC + harness. Make it opt-in via feature flag `batchpool.mode=disabled|monitor|active`.
2) Monitor-only: runtime records what it WOULD have enqueued (no change in behavior) and BatchPool collects candidate batches.
3) Hinting opt-in: BatchPool emits cache hints and the runtime may use hints for matching prefixes (opt-in per tenant).
4) Controlled active: runtime actually enqueues to BatchPool for non-hot tenants. Keep runtime local fast-path for pinned tenants.
5) Full cutover & remove in-process ad-hoc code.

nk: Love the gradual approach. Add a step to shadow traffic for 24h where requests are mirrored to BatchPool for latency and correctness tracing.

sam: Tests: we need synthetic microbench for small interactive prompts (50-100ms windows) and long-batched workloads that measure token throughput. Also correctness: ensure ordering semantics are identical.

ryan: Failure modes: BatchPool outage -> runtime fallback options: 1) local in-process batcher (safe), 2) bypass batching entirely (degraded p99). Add circuit-breaker config:```yaml
batchpool:
  circuit:
    window_ms: 30000
    p99_threshold_ms: 200
    open_duration_ms: 120000
    fallback: local|bypass
```
If open -> runtime uses `fallback`.

marta: Ops & observability: need these metrics: enqueue_rate, dequeue_rate, batch_size_p50/p95, batch_wait_ms_p99, cache_hint_hit_rate, shadow_mismatch_count. Dashboards and SLOs required.

nk: Ownership: infra-runtime builds runtime hooks + fast-path cache; infra-batching owns BatchPool service; SRE owns SLOs and alerts; devex coordinates feature flag rollout. Put this in RACI in RFC.

sam: Tech debt angle: we can finally delete the 3 separate ad-hoc batching implementations across runtime variants. Please enumerate code locations and owners in the RFC so PRs can be assigned.

ryan: Performance micro-optimizations: pack small payloads into a shared mmap buffer between runtime and BatchPool sidecar for colocated setups to avoid copies. We'll reserve that for phase 2. Keep phase 1 IPC simple (unix socket JSON) to reduce complexity.

marta: Security: BatchPool needs tenant auth and per-tenant quotas. Use mutual-TLS between runtime and BatchPool and re-use existing tenant tokens. Also ensure no cross-tenant memory sharing. Document these requirements.

nk: Rollout gating: require p50 delta < 5ms and p95 delta < 12ms on monitored tenants for 48h and zero critical shadow mismatches before moving monitor->active.

sam: Can we add a small eval harness to run model-specific prompts through the shadow path and compare outputs? That would surface nondeterministic issues introduced by batching.

ryan: Yes; tie that into our E2E tests. Also add a model-profile allowlist/denylist for batchable models (some tiny models should never be batched). Keep profiles in model-registry.

marta: Timeline: PoC + harness (2w), monitor rollout split across 2 sprints (10% -> 40%), active for long-tail tenants next sprint after that, full deprecate in-process code in 6-8 weeks depending on signals.

devops-bot: New RFC draft created: session-batcher->batchpool by marta. Link: git/repo/rfcs/0000-batchpool.md (CI: pending).

nk: I'll slot a 30m RFC walkthrough tomorrow. Please include sample payloads, telemetry schema, and the exact circuit-breaker parameters in the RFC appendix.

sam: I'll start a branch enumerating the in-process batcher locations and simple tests for ordering invariants.

marta: Thanks all. I'll post the RFC by EOD and tag infra-batching, infra-runtime, devex, and SRE. Any final nits?
